New York State Weekly Influenza/Respiratory Surveillance Report
During the week ending January 01, 2022 (MMWR Week 52) — Season 2021-22
Source PDF: 2022-01-01_flu_report.pdf
================================================================================

SUMMARY (During the week ending January 01, 2022)
- Influenza activity level was categorized as geographically widespread. This is the seventh consecutive week widespread activity has been reported.
- Laboratories tested 97,637 specimens for influenza, of which 5,075 (5.2%) were positive, an 18% decrease over last week.
- Of the 7,285 specimens submitted to WHO/NREVSS clinical laboratories, 329 (4.52%) were positive, 326 for influenza A and 3 for influenza B.
- Of the 9 specimens tested at Wadsworth Center, 3 were positive for influenza A (H3).
- The percent of patient visits for influenza-like illness (ILI) from ILINet providers was 4.18%, above the regional baseline of 3.30%.
- The number of patients hospitalized with laboratory-confirmed influenza was 291, a 7% decrease from last week.
- There were no influenza-associated pediatric deaths reported this week. There have been no influenza-associated pediatric deaths reported this season.

LABORATORY REPORTS OF INFLUENZA (INCLUDING NYC) — PART 1
For the week ending January 01, 2022, influenza activity remained geographically widespread for a seventh consecutive week. Laboratories tested 97,637 specimens, of which 5,075 (5.2%) were positive, an 18% decrease in weekly positives from the prior week (holiday-week reporting likely contributed). The county activity map shows 58 counties reporting cases this week, with incidence ranging from 0 to 238.50 cases per 100,000 population. Most counties stayed in the highest activity category statewide. Counties with smaller populations may show elevated rates when fewer than 10 confirmed cases are reported. ILI rose further above baseline (4.18%), indicating sustained intense activity through the current week despite lower test counts.

LABORATORY REPORTS OF INFLUENZA (INCLUDING NYC) — PART 2
The by-week chart (N=31,673 season-to-date) shows weekly positive reports having peaked near 9,000 in mid-December and standing at about 5,000 in the current week ending January 01; percent positive remained high near 6-8%, with influenza A dominating. By age group, 18-49 years dominates (12,405), followed by 5-17 years (11,175), 0-4 years (4,895), 50-64 (1,670) and 65+ (1,515). The incidence-by-region chart shows Metro Area highest (peaking near 85 mid-December, around 30-35 currently), with Central near 25-30. The season-comparison chart shows 2021-22 near its plateau, still below the 2019-20 peak. Trends reflect only published weeks.

WHO/NREVSS COLLABORATING LABORATORIES
The WHO/NREVSS clinical laboratories chart shows positives around 329 in the current week ending January 01, with percent positive near 4.5%; detections remain overwhelmingly "A subtyping not performed" plus influenza A (H3). This week, 329 of 7,285 clinical specimens (4.52%) were positive (326 influenza A, 3 influenza B). The public health laboratories chart shows mostly influenza A (H3) plus "A subtyping not performed." Wadsworth Center tested 9 specimens, 3 positive for influenza A (H3), with 58 H3 to date (11 ILINet, 12 FluSurv-NET). Virologic surveillance confirms continued influenza A (H3) predominance through the current week.

SUMMARY (During the week ending January 15, 2022)
- Influenza activity level was categorized as geographically widespread. This is the ninth consecutive week widespread activity has been reported.
- Laboratories tested 79,602 specimens for influenza, of which 2,338 (2.9%) were positive, a 46% decrease over last week.
- Of the 9,810 specimens submitted to WHO/NREVSS clinical laboratories, 128 (1.30%) were positive, 126 for influenza A and 2 for influenza B.
- Of the 14 specimens tested at Wadsworth Center, none were positive for influenza.
- The percent of patient visits for influenza-like illness (ILI) from ILINet providers was 2.46%, below the regional baseline of 3.30%.
- The number of patients hospitalized with laboratory-confirmed influenza was 87, a 37% decrease over last week.
- There were no influenza-associated pediatric deaths reported this week. There have been no influenza-associated pediatric deaths reported this season.

LABORATORY REPORTS OF INFLUENZA (INCLUDING NYC) — PART 1
Influenza activity remained geographically widespread for the ninth consecutive week. During the week ending January 15, 2022, 60 counties reported laboratory-confirmed influenza cases, with incidence ranging from 0 to 70.29 cases per 100,000 population. The county activity map shows cases concentrated across upstate and the metro/NYC area, with the deepest shading (highest incidence categories) in several upstate counties and New York City boroughs. The report notes that counties with smaller populations are likely to show an incidence rate greater than 10 per 100,000 even when fewer than 10 confirmed cases are reported. This week saw a 46% decline in positives from the prior week, reflecting a slowing after the season's December peak.

LABORATORY REPORTS OF INFLUENZA (INCLUDING NYC) — PART 2
Season total positives reached N=38,379. The weekly chart shows influenza A overwhelmingly dominant; positives peaked the week ending December 18, 2021 (roughly 9,000 reports, percent positive near 8%) and have stepped down through the current week ending January 15. By age, 18-49 years led (14,919), followed by 5-17 years (13,475), 0-4 years (6,679), 50-64 years (2,028), and 65+ years (1,864). Regionally, the Metro Area drove incidence highest near the December peak (about 85/100,000), with Central, NYC, Capital District, and Western lower; all regions have descended from peak through the current week. Versus prior seasons, 2021-22 peaked earlier and lower than the large 2019-20 and 2018-19 seasons.

WHO/NREVSS COLLABORATING LABORATORIES
Among WHO/NREVSS clinical laboratories, 128 of 9,810 specimens (1.30%) were positive this week (126 influenza A, 2 influenza B). The clinical-lab chart shows positive specimens and percent positive peaking around mid-December (about 400 specimens, near 6-7% positive) and declining through the current week ending January 15, with influenza A (H3) and unsubtyped A predominating. Public health laboratory data similarly peak in late November/December, dominated by A (H3) and A not subtyped. At Wadsworth Center, all 57 season-to-date influenza A viruses characterized were A (H3); the ILINet/FluSurv-NET subsets (11 outpatient, 14 inpatient) were likewise entirely A (H3), indicating a strongly H3-dominant season.

SUMMARY (During the week ending April 26, 2025)
- Influenza activity was categorized as geographically widespread. This is the 20th consecutive week of widespread activity reported this season.
- Laboratories tested 28,722 specimens for influenza, of which 4,342 (15%) were positive, a 32% decrease in positive cases compared with the previous week.
- The number of patients hospitalized with laboratory-confirmed influenza was 192, a 26% decrease in hospitalized cases compared with the previous week.
- Of the 3,853 specimens submitted to WHO/NREVSS laboratories, 339 (8.80%) were positive. 124 were positive for influenza A and 215 for influenza B.
- The percent of patient visits for influenza-like illness (ILI) from ILINet providers was 2.23%, below the epidemic threshold of 4.20%.
- There was 1 outbreak reported in a hospital and 3 outbreaks reported in nursing homes, a 69% decrease in hospital and nursing home outbreaks compared with the previous week. Season to date, a total of 1,023 outbreaks have been reported from hospitals and nursing homes in NYS.
- There were two influenza-associated pediatric deaths reported this week. 25 influenza-associated pediatric deaths have been reported this season.

LABORATORY REPORTS OF INFLUENZA (INCLUDING NYC) — PART 1
For week ending April 26, 2025, activity stayed widespread for a 20th consecutive week. Laboratories tested 28,722 specimens; 4,342 (15%) were positive, down 32% week-over-week. Season-to-date positives reached 536,107, far above 2023-24 (414,416), 2022-23 (347,250), and 2021-22 (130,687). Hospitalizations were 192, a 26% decline, with 33,241 season-to-date. The season-comparison charts show 2024-25 peaking in late January/early February and declining steadily toward the current week; it remains the largest season plotted. Two pediatric deaths were reported this week, raising the season total to 25. Both positive-case and hospitalization curves are genuinely lower now than at the winter peak, reflecting continued late-spring decline.

LABORATORY REPORTS OF INFLUENZA (INCLUDING NYC) — PART 2
60 counties reported influenza cases this week, with incidence ranging from 0 to 84.50 cases/100,000 population; the map shows broad statewide coverage with a few counties (e.g., Hamilton) reporting previously but not this week. The season tally was 6 sporadic, 1 local, 3 regional, and 20 widespread weeks. Regional positive-case incidence charts show Metro Area peaking highest (~400/100,000) in late January, NYC next (~290), with all five regions well past their winter peak and declining toward the current week. Hospitalization incidence by region similarly peaked near late January/early February and is now declining through the current week across Capital, Central, Western, Metro, and NYC.

WHO/NREVSS COLLABORATING LABORATORIES
Of 3,853 specimens submitted to WHO/NREVSS laboratories, 339 (8.80%) were positive: 124 influenza A and 215 influenza B, confirming late-season B predominance. The subtype chart shows the winter peak dominated by influenza A (subtyping not performed) and A(H3), with influenza B Victoria a larger share toward spring. Percent positive peaked above 25-30% near the winter apex and has declined to under 9% at the current week. Healthcare-associated outbreaks week-to-date totaled 4 (Statewide: 1 hospital, 3 nursing home), with 1,023 season-to-date. The plotted specimen bars and percent-positive line genuinely decline from the earlier peak through the current week.
